correctness.rationale: On the fixed 2m vertices an (m−1)-edge matching leaves two vertices, so its only possible perfect-matching extension uses their edge. For each relative perfect matching delete an edge other than one missing from G. The resulting face is free and still relative; the pairs cannot intersect. Removing them fixes the subcomplex and kills the relative chains in degree m−1. The relative homology in degree m−2 is then a subgroup of a free group, so the pair sequence proves injection and a free cokernel. The same absolute collapse proves freeness for each stage, including graphs with no perfect matchings; choosing successive complements gives a simultaneous filtered basis. An independent verifier reconstructed the finite Morse certificates as acyclic full Hasse orientations with one critical vertex and respectively 79 and 132 critical two-cells, and confirmed the 45 relative pairs. For based maps between these sphere wedges, Hurewicz classifies the map on each summand by the integral homology matrix; primitivity brings this to the standard inclusion by realizable basis changes. Cofibration and mapping-cone invariance give the wedge of 53 two-spheres. The two free triangle collapses in the connected six-cycle example leave a graph of cycle rank two mapping into a simply connected target complex.
residual_risks: Finite Morse certificates pertain only to the concrete examples; the universal inclusion uses the relative-collapse proof.
